newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS sees up to four percent growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: SAS sees up to four percent growth in 97.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Monday that despite its cost-cutting programme and closing of unprofitable routes it intended to increase volume and market share.
"SAS is not talking about reducing production, on the contrary expansion of between three and four percent is planned for 1997," SAS director Vagn Soerensen wrote in the in-house journal Inside SAS.
"This is growth on a par with the European average for this year and also an expression of the fact that SAS is on the offensive and seeks to increase its market share," he added.

Soerensen was confident that SAS could meet the intense competition unleashed by European deregulation, saying that the company --owned jointly by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and by private investors -- intended not only to cut costs but to increase earnings.
"Competition is intensifying, but if we play our cards cleverly and exploit all our resources we can acquit ourselves well in absolutely any situation," he said.

SAS pledged to slash costs after a 46 percent slump in pre-tax profits to 1.26 billion Swedish crowns ($184 million) in the first nine months of 1996. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969653
